newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks end at record closing high.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks end at record closing high.

text.p: Australian shares finished at a record close on Monday after rising modestly from the open following the continued strength of the Dow which achieved another record high close on Friday.
The benchmark All Ordinaries index closed 11.3 points higher at 2,394.7, two points higher than its previous record close of 2,392.7, set on Thursday last week.
Volume was thin and dealers said a lack of company news resulted in low activity from disinterested investors.
"It was always going to be stronger today - the banks and resource sectors led the market again," said Jamie Spiteri, a dealer at Sydney firm, Shaw Stockbroking.
Spiteri said the 2400 level was still proving to be a significant barrier for the market.
"I think stronger base metal prices combined with a weaker local currency would help the market past this level," he said.
National Australia Bank was the most outstanding blue chip issue on the day, finishing 22 cents higher at A$14.55 (US$11.79) after touching an all-time high of A$14.59 during the session.
The market ended off its highs after bonds weakened following a third quarter capital expenditure report which came in stronger than expected.
Capital expenditure rose a seasonally adjusted 0.9 percent in the September quarter compared with median forecasts for a 3.0 percent fall.
